Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:10:1.hebrew: גמ' - סברות וטעמי סתימתיהן של משניות, ולתרצם במה שסותרות זו את זו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:10:1.english: Gemara - The logical reasoning and the reasons behind the anonymous [rulings] of the Mishnayot, and reconciling them where they contradict each other.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:10:2.english: For days - The days of the week.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:11:1.english: Therefore they were called, etc. - This is an independent matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:11:2.hebrew: נקראו ראשונים סופרים - כדכתיב (ד"ה א ב): ״ומשפחות סופרים יושבי יעבץ״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:11:2.english: The earlier [generations] were called soferim - As it is written (I Chronicles 2:55): “And the families of scribes who dwelt at Jabez.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:12:1.english: The vav of gaḥon - [As in the verse:] “Whatever goes on its belly” (Leviticus 11:42).

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:12:2.english: They did not move from there - It is not explained where [this occurred].

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:14:1.english: Fewer than it - Than the count of a Torah scroll.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:15:1.hebrew: יהו מחודדין בפיך - חזור עליהם ובדוק בעומקם, שאם ישאלך אדם, לא תצטרך לגמגם, אלא שתוכל לומר מיד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:15:1.english: They should be sharp in your mouth - Review them and examine their depth, so that if a person asks you, you will not need to stutter, but rather you will be able to answer immediately.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא ליה לשטן גירא בעיניך - כלומר, הייתי מתגרה בו. ושטן הוא יצר הרע, ולא אירא שיחטיאני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:1.english: I would say to Satan: An arrow in your eye - That is to say, I would provoke him. And Satan is the evil inclination, [meaning:] and I do not fear that he will cause me to sin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:2.hebrew: אדידך על צוארי דבריך - בעוד ידך תקיפה על בנך, קודם שיגדיל ולא יקבל תוכחתך — השיאו אשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:2.english: While your hand is on your son’s neck - While your hand is [still] firm over your son, before he grows up and will not accept your rebuke — marry him to a wife.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:3.hebrew: משיתסר - שנין, הגיע זמן לכנוס, ויותר מעשרין ותרתין אל תאחרהו. לשון אחר: "אדידך על צוארי דבריך" — בשעה שעוד ידך תקיפה עליו, הוי זהיר ללמדו תוכחות. ואיזה זמנו? משיתסר ועד עשרים ותרתין. בציר משיתסר אין בו דעת לקבל תוכחות כל כך, ואל תכביד יסורין ותוכחות; ויותר מעשרים ותרתין יש לחוש שלא יבעט. וזה עיקר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:1:3.english: From sixteen - [Sixteen] years: the time has arrived [for him] to marry, and beyond twenty-two [years], do not delay him. Another explanation: "While your hand is on your son’s neck" — while your hand is still firm over him, be careful to teach him reproofs. And what is its timeframe? From sixteen until twenty-two. [At] less than sixteen, he does not have enough understanding to accept reproofs so much, and do not make chastisements and reproofs heavy; and beyond twenty-two, there is concern lest he rebel. And this is the primary [explanation].

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:2:1.hebrew: על פי דרכו - דרך שכל ימיו יהא מתנהג בו, חנוך לו בנערותו. ואיזוהי נערותו? רבי יהודה ורבי נחמיה כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:2:1.english: According to his way - The way in which he should conduct himself all his days, train him [in it] during his youth. And which [period] is his youth? Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:3:1.english: Zevulun ben Dan - A student who was in their days.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:3:2.hebrew: אינו מלמדו משנה - אין חובת בנו עליו אלא במקרא. מכאן ואילך, ילמד הוא לעצמו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:3:2.english: He does not teach him Mishna - The obligation [to teach] his son is upon him only for Scripture; from here onward, he must learn on his own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:3:3.english: Torah - And not Prophets and Writings.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:4:1.hebrew: כזבולון בן דן שלמדו אבי אביו - ועד היכן נמי דקאמרי', הכי קאמרי': עד היכן אדם חייב ללמוד תורה בדורותיו? אמר רב יהודה: לבנו ולבן בנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:4:1.english: Like Zevulun ben Dan, whose father’s father taught him - And as for [the question] “To what extent” that we also said, this is what we were saying: “To what extent is a person obligated to teach Torah down through his generations?” Rav Yehuda said: “To his son and to his grandson.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:1.hebrew: דשדי דיסנא ארישיה - סדין שאינו ראוי לעטיפת הראש, אלא כסוי בעלמא, שם על ראשו שלא לילך בגילוי ראשו, ולא הספיק להתעטף בסודרו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:1.english: That he placed a cloth on his head - A sheet that is not suitable for wrapping the head, but rather a mere covering, he placed upon his head so as not to walk bareheaded, and he did not have time to wrap himself in his scarf.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:2.english: What is all this - That you hurried to go out without the [head] wrapping befitting you:

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:3.hebrew: לא טעים אומצא - בשר מעט בגחלים, היו רגילין לטעום בבקר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:3.english: Would not taste meat - A little meat [broiled] on coals, [which] they were accustomed to taste in the morning.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:4.hebrew: עד דמקרי לינוקא ומוספיה - מהדר לו מה שקרא אתמול, ומלמדו עוד פסוק יותר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:8:4.english: Until he read with the child and added to it - He reviews with him what he read yesterday, and teaches him one more verse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:9:1.hebrew: אלא ושלשתם - מדלא כתיב ושניתם, שישלישם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 30a:9:1.english: Rather, veshillashtam - Since it is not written veshinitam, [it is expounded] that one should divide them into three.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:10:1.hebrew: לא צריכא ליומי - פירש בקונטרס: ימי השבת, כלומר: שני ימים מקרא, ושני ימים משנה, ושני ימים גמרא. ולא נהירא, דא"כ — אכתי הוה מצי למיפרך: "מי ידע כמה חיי?!" ונ"ל לפרש: בכל יום ויום עצמו ישלש. על כן תיקן בסדר רב עמרם גאון, כמו שאנו נוהגים בכל יום קודם פסוקי דזמרה, לומר מקרא, ומשנה, וגמרא. ור"ת פי' שאנו סומכין אהא דאמרינן בסנהדרין (דף כד.): "בבל — בלולה במקרא, במשנה, ובגמרא", דגמרת בבל בלול מכולם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:10:1.english: "No, it is necessary for days" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: The days of the week; meaning to say, two days [devoted to] Bible, two days [to] Mishnah, and two days [to] Gemara. But this is not clear, for if so, [the Gemara] could still have objected: "Who knows the length of his life?" And it appears to me to explain: One should divide each and every day itself into three. Therefore, [Rav Amram Gaon] instituted in Seder Rav Amram Gaon, as we are accustomed [to do] each day before Pesukei DeZimra, to recite Bible, Mishnah, and Gemara. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that we rely on that which we say in Sanhedrin (24a): "Bavel is mixed with Bible, with Mishnah, and with Gemara" — for the Babylonian Talmud is mixed with all of them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:11:1.hebrew: נקראו סופרים - פי' בקונטרס: כדכתיב "ומשפחות סופרים יושבי יעבץ". ובירושלמי (שקלים פ"ה) מפרש, שעשו כל התורה כולה מספרות — כגון: אבות מלאכות ארבעים חסר אחת (שבת דף עג.), וארבעה אבות נזיקין (ב"ק דף ב.), וכיוצא בהם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:11:1.english: "[They] were called soferim" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explains: As it is written, “And the families of scribes who dwelt at Jabez” (I Chronicles 2:55). And in the Yerushalmi (Shekalim, chapter 5), it explains that they made the entire Torah into numerical categories — such as: forty minus one primary categories of labor (Shabbat 73a), and four primary categories of damage (Bava Kamma 2a), and the like.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:14:1.hebrew: [יתר עליו תהלים שמונה כו' - תימה, דע"כ בחומש יש יותר; דאפילו אם יהיו פסוקי תהלים מג' תיבות בלבד, אינו כ"כ כמו שיש בחומש. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:14:1.english: ["Psalms has eight more [verses] than that, etc." - It is astonishing, for perforce there are more [verses] in the Chumash, as even if the verses of Psalms were of only three words, it would not be as many as there are in the Chumash. — Tosafot Yeshanim]:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:15:1.hebrew: אל תגמגם ותאמר לו - והא דאמר באלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כג:) דצורבא מרבנן משני בדיבוריה במסכ', אומר ר"ת: דהיינו אם שואלים אותו אם למדת מסכת זו, אל יתגאה לומר שלמדה — כלומר, למדתי הרבה. אבל אם שואלים אותו דבר הלכה, או שצריכין ללמוד ממנו מסכ', צריך שיהיו מחודדים בפיו, שלא יגמגם בדבר. ולא דמי להא דאמר (מסכת ד"א זוטא פ"ג): "למד לשונך לומר איני יודע, שמא תתבדה ותאחז" — דהיינו במילי דעלמא; ואפילו בדברי תורה, לא יאמר "יודע אני דבר" להתפאר בו בכך, אלא מה שיודע יורה וילמוד לתלמידים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 30a:15:1.english: “Do not stutter and say to him” - And as for that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Elu Metzi’ot (Bava Metzia 23b), that a Torah scholar may alter his speech regarding a tractate — Rabbeinu Tam says that this is [only] if they ask him, “Did you learn this tractate?” He should not boastfully say that he learned it, meaning: “I have learned [it] thoroughly.” But if they ask him a matter of Halakhah, or if they need to learn a tractate from him, [words of Torah] must be sharp in his mouth so that he does not stutter over the matter. And it is not comparable to that which is said (Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, ch. 3): “Teach your tongue to say ‘I do not know,’ lest you be refuted and caught [by your words]” — for that is regarding worldly matters; and even in matters of Torah, he should not say, “I know something,” to boast about it in that way, but rather what he knows he should rule and teach to students.
